description.en: The band front lateral raise combines elements of the front raise and lateral raise into one motion using a resistance band. By raising the band ends out at a 45-degree angle, you hit both the front and side delts simultaneously. It is a strong combo movement for shoulder development.

en: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grip the band ends in each hand at your thighs.
Maintain a slight bend in the elbows throughout.
Brace your core and stand tall.
Raise both band ends out and forward at about a 45-degree angle.
Continue until your hands reach shoulder height.
Squeeze your front and side delts at the top.
Lower the bands back down with control to the starting position.
Hits front and side delts in one motion
Time-efficient shoulder training
Constant band tension through the range
Builds shoulder size and definition
Useful for home training
Easy to scale by changing band tension

description.en: The band kneeling lat pulldown uses a resistance band anchored overhead while you kneel facing the anchor. Pulling the band ends down to your shoulders trains the lats with constant band tension. The kneeling position eliminates leg drive and isolates the upper body work.

en: Anchor a resistance band overhead at a high point.
Kneel facing the anchor with both knees on the floor.
Grip the band ends in each hand with arms extended overhead.
Brace your core and sit tall.
Pull the bands down to your shoulders by driving your elbows back and down.
Squeeze your lats hard at the bottom of the pull.
Slowly extend your arms back overhead to the starting position.
Maintain the kneeling position throughout the entire set.
Trains lats without a cable machine
Constant band tension through the range
Kneeling position eliminates leg drive
Builds lat size and strength
Useful for home training
Easy to scale by changing band tension

description.en: The band standing external shoulder rotation is a rotator cuff strengthening drill that uses a resistance band. The lifter anchors the band at the side and rotates the forearm outward against band tension. It builds shoulder health and stability.

en: Anchor a resistance band at elbow height.
Stand sideways to the anchor with the working arm furthest away.
Grip the band handle with the elbow tucked at the side.
Bend the elbow at ninety degrees with the forearm across the body.
Brace your core and keep the elbow pinned.
Rotate the forearm outward away from the body.
Hold briefly at the rotated position.
Return with control. Finish all reps then switch sides.
Builds the rotator cuff
Strong shoulder health move
Trains external rotation
Useful warm-up
Builds shoulder stability

description.en: The barbell front rack walking lunge combines the walking lunge pattern with the front rack position. The bar held across the front shoulders forces an upright torso while you step forward into alternating lunges. The combination builds quad strength, core stability, and is a strong CrossFit-style conditioning movement.

en: Position a barbell across the front of your shoulders in the front rack position.
Keep your elbows high and chest up.
Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Brace your core hard.
Step forward with your right leg into a forward lunge.
Lower until your back knee approaches the floor.
Drive through the front heel to step forward into the next lunge with the left leg.
Continue walking forward with alternating lunges.
Front rack hold emphasizes quads and core
Walking pattern adds conditioning
Forces upright torso
Builds single-leg strength
Strong functional carryover
Useful for CrossFit-style training

description.en: The barbell straight-leg deadlift (stiff-leg deadlift) is a hip hinge exercise performed with the legs kept as straight as possible. The minimal knee bend places maximum demand on the hamstrings throughout the lift. It is one of the most effective hamstring builders.

en: Stand with feet hip-width apart. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip in front of your thighs.
Stand tall. Keep your legs as straight as possible (just a soft knee bend to avoid locking).
Brace your core. Pull your shoulders back.
Hinge at the hips, pushing your butt back. Lower the bar along your legs.
Continue until you feel a deep hamstring stretch (usually mid-shin or below).
Drive your hips forward to stand. Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Maintain a flat back throughout — never round.
Use moderate weight. Aim for 8 to 12 reps.
Maximum hamstring loading through full range
Builds posterior chain strength
Develops hamstring flexibility
Teaches hip hinge mechanics
Easy to load progressively
Excellent for hamstring hypertrophy

description.en: The bodyweight frog pump is a high rep glute burnout where the lifter lies on the floor with the soles of the feet pressed together and the knees out wide. The hips pump up and down rapidly to burn out the glutes. It is a great finisher.

en: Lie flat on the floor on your back.
Press the soles of your feet together with knees out wide.
Position your feet a foot or two from your hips.
Place your hands at your sides for support.
Brace your core and tuck your chin slightly.
Drive through the outer edges of your feet to lift your hips up.
Squeeze the glutes hard at the top of each pump.
Lower the hips back down and pump up again rapidly.
High rep glute burnout
No equipment required
Hits outer glutes hard
Useful glute finisher
Easy to add to any session
Strong glute hypertrophy move

description.en: The bottle hammer curl uses filled water bottles or jugs as makeshift weights for the hammer curl pattern. Holding a heavy bottle in each hand with a neutral grip, you curl them up to shoulder height. The neutral grip targets the brachialis for arm thickness.

en: Fill two water bottles or jugs with water or sand for resistance.
Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a bottle in each hand at your sides with palms facing each other.
Pin your elbows against your sides.
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back.
Curl both bottles up by bending only at the elbows, keeping the neutral grip.
Continue until the bottles reach shoulder height.
Squeeze the biceps and brachialis at the top, then lower with control.
Trains hammer curls with no traditional weights
Hammer grip targets brachialis
Builds arm thickness
Useful for home or travel training
Easy to scale by changing bottle weight
Strong forearm engagement

description.en: The cable goblet squat is a squat variation performed with a rope or D-handle attached to a low cable pulley, held at the chest like a goblet. The cable provides a forward-pulling force that challenges anti-tip core stability while the squat builds the quads and glutes. It is unique because cable resistance peaks at standing, opposite to free-weight squats.

en: Attach a rope handle to a low cable pulley.
Stand facing the cable. Grip both ends of the rope and hold it at your chest like a goblet.
Step back to create cable tension. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Brace your core hard. The cable will pull you forward — resist this throughout.
Sit back and down into a squat. Keep your torso upright.
Descend until thighs are parallel or deeper.
Drive through your feet to stand back up. The cable resistance peaks at the standing position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Constant cable tension throughout the squat
Resistance peaks at standing (opposite of free weights)
Trains anti-tip core stability
Useful when no dumbbells or kettlebells are available
Easy to load progressively
Beginner-friendly squat variation

description.en: The cable judo flip is a rotational core exercise where you grip a high cable with both hands and pull it diagonally across your body in a motion that simulates a judo throw or wood chop. It builds explosive rotational power, oblique strength, and shoulder stability.

en: Set a cable pulley to a high position. Attach a rope or single handle.
Stand sideways to the cable with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grip the handle with both hands. Start with arms extended above your head toward the cable.
Pull the cable diagonally across your body from high to low — like a judo throw.
Rotate your torso, drive through your hips, and finish with the handle near your opposite knee.
Control the cable back to the starting position over two seconds.
Complete reps on one side, then switch sides.
Use moderate weight. Aim for 10 to 12 reps per side.
Builds explosive rotational power
Targets the obliques heavily
Carries over to martial arts and rotational sports
Constant cable tension throughout
Easy to load progressively
Trains hip-to-shoulder force transfer

description.en: The cable standing chest press is a chest exercise performed standing in a split stance with two cable pulleys behind you, pressing the handles forward simultaneously. The standing position adds significant core engagement, while the cables provide constant tension throughout. It is a functional chest exercise that translates to real-world pushing patterns.

en: Set two cable pulleys at chest height. Attach D-handles to each.
Stand between the cables with your back to the machine. Grip both handles.
Step forward into a split stance — one foot forward for stability.
Bring the handles to your chest with elbows bent and tucked at roughly 45 degrees.
Press both handles forward simultaneously, extending your arms straight in front.
Squeeze your chest hard at the lockout. Your hands should converge slightly in front.
Slowly return the handles to your chest under control. Maintain cable tension throughout.
Brace your core hard — the standing position demands stability.
Constant cable tension throughout
Standing position adds core engagement
Functional pushing pattern
Bilateral movement allows heavier loading
Easy to load progressively
Trains chest with stability demand

description.en: The dumbbell bent arm iso hold is a static biceps exercise where dumbbells are held at a 90 degree elbow position for an extended time. The isometric hold builds biceps endurance, forearm strength, and grip stamina. It is a useful finisher and accessory for arm training.

en: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Curl the dumbbells up to a 90 degree elbow position.
Pin your elbows against your sides.
Keep your palms facing up and the dumbbells just above the elbows.
Brace your core and keep your shoulders down.
Hold this static position with the biceps under tension.
Breathe steadily and resist any sag in the arms.
Lower the dumbbells with control to finish the set.
Builds static biceps strength
Improves arm endurance
Strengthens grip and forearms
Useful biceps finisher
Builds tendon resilience
No fancy equipment needed

description.en: The dumbbell half kneeling lift and chop is a core builder that uses a dumbbell in a half kneeling stance. The lifter performs diagonal lift and chop patterns to train the obliques and anti-rotation core. It is a strong functional core move.

en: Kneel in a half kneeling position with one knee down.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands at the down knee side.
Brace your core and keep the chest up.
Lift the dumbbell diagonally up and across the body.
Finish with the dumbbell overhead on the opposite side.
Reverse the path back down to the starting position.
Keep the hips square throughout.
Finish all reps then switch sides.
Trains the obliques
Builds anti-rotation core
Strong functional move
Useful core builder
Builds rotational power

description.en: The dumbbell incline alternate reverse fly is performed face down on an incline bench, raising the dumbbells one arm at a time. The chest support eliminates lower back stress while the alternating pattern increases time under tension on each side. It is a strong choice for strict rear delt isolation.

en: Set an incline bench to about 30 to 45 degrees.
Lie face down on the bench with chest supported.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms hanging below shoulders, palms facing each other.
Maintain a slight bend in the elbows throughout.
Brace your core.
Raise the right dumbbell out to the side to shoulder height.
Squeeze the right rear delt at the top, then lower with control.
Repeat with the left arm. Alternate sides each rep.
Strict rear delt isolation
Chest support eliminates body english
Alternating pattern increases time under tension
Builds posterior shoulder strength
Improves posture
Useful for shoulder balance work

description.en: The dumbbell lying supination (side-lying external rotation) lies on your side with your top elbow pinned against your body and rotates a light dumbbell upward. It targets the infraspinatus and teres minor — the external rotators of the shoulder. It is a gold-standard rotator cuff exercise.

en: Lie on your left side. Hold a light dumbbell in your right hand.
Bend your right elbow to 90 degrees. Pin your right elbow against your right side.
Start with the dumbbell pointing toward the floor in front of your stomach.
Rotate your forearm upward (external rotation) while keeping your elbow pinned.
Rotate until your forearm is nearly vertical.
Slowly lower back to start.
Complete reps, then switch sides.
Use very light weight. Aim for 15 to 20 reps per side.
Gold-standard external rotation exercise
Targets the infraspinatus and teres minor
Essential for shoulder health
Prevents rotator cuff injuries
Simple side-lying setup
Used in physical therapy worldwide

description.en: The dumbbell one leg fly on exercise ball is a chest fly performed on a stability ball with one leg lifted. The lifter lies on the ball, lifts one foot off the floor, and performs a fly with both arms. The single leg base adds brutal core and balance demand.

en: Sit on a stability ball and walk the feet out so the upper back rests on the ball.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand and press them up over the chest.
Lift one foot off the floor.
Brace your core hard and keep the hips lifted.
Lower the dumbbells out wide to the sides in a fly arc.
Continue until the upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Squeeze the chest to bring the dumbbells back over the chest.
Switch legs between sets.
Strong chest builder
Adds core challenge
Trains balance
Builds chest size
Strong dumbbell move
Useful chest builder

description.en: The dumbbell seated on exercise ball shoulder press is an overhead press performed seated on a stability ball. The unstable surface forces extra core engagement while the shoulders and triceps press the dumbbells overhead. It is a strong functional shoulder builder.

en: Sit on a stability ball with feet planted on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder level with palms facing forward.
Sit tall with chest up and core braced hard.
Press both dumbbells straight up over your head.
Lock out the arms at the top.
Pause briefly with the dumbbells over your shoulders.
Lower with control back to shoulder level.
Keep your torso steady and stable throughout.
Builds shoulders and triceps
Trains core stability
Recruits stabilizers
Improves balance
Strict seated form
Useful functional press

description.en: The dumbbell seated preacher curl performs bicep curls with one dumbbell with the back of your upper arm braced on a preacher bench pad. The preacher position eliminates cheating and places the biceps at a slight stretch, making every rep strict.

en: Sit at a preacher bench. Place the back of your right upper arm on the pad.
Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with a supinated (palm-up) grip.
Start with your arm extended — biceps stretched.
Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
Squeeze your biceps at the top.
Lower under control — do not let your arm fully relax at the bottom.
Complete reps, then switch arms.
Use moderate weight. Aim for 10 to 12 reps per side.
Preacher pad ensures strict isolation
Places biceps at a stretch at the bottom
Eliminates all body english
Unilateral exposes imbalances
Builds bicep size
Easy to progress

description.en: The dumbbells sumo squat is a wide-stance squat where you hold a single heavy dumbbell vertically with both hands between your legs and squat down to bring it close to the floor. The wide stance shifts emphasis to the adductors and inner-glute regions while still building the quads.

en: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out 30 to 45 degrees.
Hold one heavy dumbbell vertically with both hands underneath the top end. Let it hang between your legs.
Brace your core. Lift your chest. Pull your shoulders back.
Sit your hips back and down. Keep your chest tall throughout.
Lower until the dumbbell almost touches the floor or your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Keep your knees pushed wide tracking over your toes.
Drive through your full feet to stand. Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Repeat for the desired reps. Use heavy weight — the wide stance allows it.
Heavy adductor engagement
Builds quads and glutes
Allows heavy loading with one dumbbell
No barbell needed
Easier on the lower back than back squats
Excellent for inner-thigh development

description.en: The ez bar front twist raise is a front raise variation with a wrist twist. The lifter starts with the bar at the thighs in a pronated grip then lifts it up while rotating the wrists to a neutral grip. The rotation adds forearm engagement to the delt raise.

en: Stand tall with an ez curl bar in front of the thighs.
Grip the bar with a pronated overhand grip on the inner curves.
Brace your core and set the chest tall.
Keep the elbows slightly bent throughout.
Raise the bar straight up in front while rotating the wrists.
Finish with the bar at shoulder height with palms facing each other.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower the bar back down rotating the wrists back to pronated.
Strong front delt builder
Trains forearm rotation
Combo shoulder and grip move
Useful shoulder builder
Strong ez bar move
Builds wrist control

description.en: The forward pulse lunge with hands overhead is a bodyweight leg burner that adds small pulse reps in a forward lunge while holding the arms overhead. The overhead position challenges core and shoulder stability.

en: Stand tall and step forward into a long lunge stance.
Lower into a deep lunge with the back knee close to the floor.
Raise both arms straight overhead with biceps near the ears.
Brace the core and keep the chest tall.
Pulse a few inches up and down within the lunge bottom range.
Keep the front shin vertical and the torso upright through every pulse.
Maintain the overhead arm position throughout the pulses.
Complete all pulses on one side then switch legs.
Smokes the quads and glutes through repeated pulses.
Challenges core stability with arms overhead.
Improves shoulder mobility and overhead control.
Builds isometric leg strength in the lunge bottom.
Improves single leg balance and coordination.
No equipment needed.

description.en: The hip clam shell is a side-lying glute medius activator. The lifter lies on the side with the knees bent and feet stacked, then lifts the top knee while keeping the feet together. The move isolates the gluteus medius and is a key hip warm-up.

en: Lie on your side with the legs stacked.
Bend the knees to about 90 degrees.
Stack the feet on top of each other.
Rest the head on your bottom arm.
Keep the feet together as you lift the top knee.
Open the knee like a clam shell to the top.
Squeeze the glute medius at the top.
Lower with control. Complete reps and switch sides.
Activates the glute medius
Builds hip stability
Useful warm-up move
No equipment needed
Easy to add to any session
Strong hip activator

description.en: The inverted wide to narrow row is an inverted row that alternates grip widths. The lifter rows with a wide grip then narrows the grip and rows again. The grip changes train the back from multiple angles in one set.

en: Set a bar at hip height.
Grip the bar with a wide overhand grip.
Hang under the bar with the body angled.
Set the body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and pinch the shoulder blades.
Pull the chest toward the bar with wide grip.
Lower then move the hands narrow and row again.
Continue alternating wide and narrow grip rows.
Trains multiple angles
Builds the back
Strong row variation
Useful for back size
Trains the biceps
No weights needed

description.en: The iron cross plank holds a plank position with arms extended wide to the sides (like a cross) rather than directly below the shoulders. The wide arm position dramatically increases chest, shoulder, and core demand compared to a standard plank.

en: Lie face down on the floor. Extend both arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
Press through your palms and toes to lift your body off the floor into a plank.
Your body should be straight from heels to head — arms extended wide.
Hold this position. The wide arms make it extremely demanding.
Breathe steadily. Maintain the plank.
Start with 10 to 15 seconds and build up.
If too difficult, start with hands slightly closer than full cross.
Maintain a flat back — do not let hips sag.
Extreme chest and shoulder demand from wide arm position
Builds isometric chest and core strength
Advanced plank progression
No equipment needed
Develops shoulder stability
Builds mental toughness

description.en: The kettlebell banded swing combines the standard kettlebell swing with a resistance band looped through the kettlebell handle and anchored to the floor. The band tension increases as the kettlebell swings up, forcing harder hip drive at the top. The combination builds explosive hip power with progressive resistance.

en: Anchor a resistance band to the floor in front of you.
Loop the band through the handle of a kettlebell.
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Grip the kettlebell handle with both hands.
Hinge at the hips and swing the kettlebell back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward explosively to swing the kettlebell up.
The band tension will increase as the kettlebell rises.
Allow the kettlebell to swing back through your legs and repeat the swing.
Forces harder hip drive at the top
Combines kettlebell load with band tension
Builds explosive hip power
Trains the posterior chain
Accommodating resistance through the swing
Useful for breaking through swing plateaus

description.en: The kneeling lat stretch on bench is a deep mobility exercise where you kneel in front of a flat bench, place your forearms on it with palms together, and sink your chest toward the floor. The bench position deepens the lat and shoulder stretch beyond what unsupported variations can achieve.

en: Kneel on the floor in front of a flat bench. Hips above knees.
Place both forearms on the bench with palms facing each other. Elbows shoulder-width apart.
Walk your knees back so your hips move further from the bench but your forearms stay on it.
Lower your chest and head down between your arms toward the floor.
Press your hips back toward your heels. Keep your back flat — do not round it.
Feel the deep stretch through your lats, shoulders, and upper back.
Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply and let gravity deepen the stretch.
To exit, walk your knees forward and rise.
Deep lat and shoulder stretch with bench support
Improves overhead mobility
Decompresses the spine
Counteracts hunched posture
Excellent warm-up before pull-ups or pressing
Easy to set up

description.en: The landmine one leg stiff leg deadlift is a single leg RDL done with a barbell anchored in a landmine. The lifter holds the loaded end with one hand and hinges on one leg. The arc shaped resistance trains the hamstrings and glutes with a unique pattern.

en: Anchor a barbell in a landmine attachment.
Stand on one leg facing the loaded end.
Grip the loaded end with the opposite hand.
Brace your core and keep the chest up.
Hinge at the hip and lift the back leg behind you.
Lower the bar toward the floor as the back leg rises.
Keep the back flat and the hips square.
Stand back up. Finish all reps then switch sides.
Builds the posterior chain
Trains balance
Loads single leg hinge
Strong landmine variation
Useful functional move

description.en: The landmine Romanian deadlift is a hip-hinge variation performed holding the end of a barbell secured in a landmine attachment. The angled bar path guides the movement and reduces the balance demand compared to a standard RDL, while providing constant tension throughout. It is an excellent variation for lifters who need more stability on the RDL.

en: Set up a barbell in a landmine attachment (or wedge the end into a corner).
Stand facing the barbell, holding the free end with both hands at hip height.
Feet hip-width apart. Set a soft, fixed bend in your knees.
Hinge at the hips by pushing your butt back. Lower the bar along the guided arc.
Keep your back flat and the bar close to your body.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up. Squeeze glutes at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
Guided bar path reduces balance demand vs standard RDL
Constant tension through the angled resistance
Builds the hamstrings and glutes effectively
More accessible for beginners learning the RDL
Easy to set up with a landmine or corner
Good variation for lifters with balance issues

description.en: The lying alternate frog kick is a core drill done lying on the back. The mover alternates pulling each heel in toward the glutes in a frog kick motion. It builds the lower abs and trains hip flexor control.

en: Lie on the back with the legs straight.
Place the hands at the sides palms down.
Brace your core and lift the legs slightly off the floor.
Bend one knee and pull the heel toward the glute.
Extend the leg back out straight.
Repeat with the other leg in alternating fashion.
Keep both feet off the floor throughout.
Continue alternating sides.
Loads the lower abs
Trains the hip flexors
Strong core drill
Builds the abs
Useful core move

description.en: The lever lying leg curl is a single-joint isolation exercise performed on a lying leg curl machine. Lying face down with the heels above a padded roller, you bend your knees to curl the weight up by contracting the hamstrings. The prone position places the hamstrings in a fully shortened (peak contraction) position at the top, providing a different stimulus from the seated version.

en: Lie face down on the lying leg curl machine. Adjust the ankle pad so it sits across the back of your lower legs, just above your heels.
Position your knees just past the edge of the bench so they can pivot freely.
Grip the handles in front of the bench and brace your core. Keep your hips pressed firmly against the pad.
Curl your heels up toward your butt by bending only at the knees.
Continue until your knees are fully bent. Squeeze your hamstrings hard for one second at the top.
Lower the pad under control over two to three seconds back to the starting position with legs nearly straight.
Stop just before the weight stack touches down to maintain tension on the hamstrings.
Avoid lifting your hips off the pad to use body english — strict form is critical.
Direct hamstring isolation with peak contraction at the top
Allows safe, comfortable training to muscular failure
Easy to load progressively in small increments
Builds the biceps femoris (knee-flexion specialist) heavily
Excellent accessory after squats or deadlifts
Trains the hamstrings without spinal load

description.en: The lever assisted chin up uses an assisted pull up machine that provides counterweight assistance during a chin up. By selecting the assistance weight, you can perform chin ups with progressively less help as you build strength. It is a strong stepping stone to bodyweight chin ups.

en: Set the assisted pull up machine with appropriate counterweight.
Stand on the kneeling pad or platform.
Grip the chin up handles with palms facing you (underhand grip).
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back.
Pull your body up by bending at the elbows and driving them down.
Continue until your chin clears the bar level.
Squeeze your back and biceps at the top.
Lower yourself back down with control to a full hang.
Builds chin up strength with controlled assistance
Stepping stone to bodyweight chin ups
Easy to scale by changing assistance
Strong lat and bicep engagement
Useful for beginners or rehab
Develops pulling strength progressively

description.en: The prone cobra hands interlocked is a back extension and chest opener done lying face down. The mover interlocks the hands behind the back and lifts the chest while pulling the arms back. It opens the chest and strengthens the upper back.

en: Lie face down on the floor.
Interlock the hands behind the lower back.
Brace your core and squeeze the glutes.
Lift the chest off the floor.
Pull the interlocked hands down toward the feet.
Squeeze the upper back and rear delts.
Hold the cobra position briefly.
Lower with control to the start.
Opens the chest
Builds the upper back
Strong cobra variation
Useful for posture
Builds back extension

description.en: Pyramid Pose (Parsvottanasana) is a standing forward fold performed in a split stance, folding the torso over the front leg. It intensely stretches the hamstrings and calves of the front leg while stretching the hip flexors of the back leg. It also challenges balance and trains spinal flexibility.

en: Stand with feet about three feet apart in a split stance. Right foot forward, left foot back and angled slightly outward.
Square your hips forward as much as possible. Both legs straight.
Inhale and lift your chest. Place your hands on your hips or clasp them behind your back.
Exhale and fold forward from the hips over your right leg. Lead with your chest, not your head.
Lower your torso as far as your flexibility allows. Place your hands on the floor, blocks, or your shin.
Keep both legs straight. Press through the heel of your front foot.
Hold for 5 to 10 breaths. Breathe deeply and let gravity deepen the fold.
Inhale to rise up. Switch sides.
Intensely stretches the hamstrings and calves of the front leg
Stretches the hip flexors of the back leg
Improves balance and proprioception
Builds spinal flexibility
Strengthens the legs isometrically
Calming forward fold

description.en: The resistance band bird dog adds external resistance to the standard bird dog by looping a band around one hand and the opposite foot. As you extend the arm and leg, the band pulls them toward center, demanding greater core anti-rotation and stabilizer strength.

en: Get on hands and knees in tabletop position.
Loop a resistance band around your right hand and left foot.
Brace your core. Keep your back flat.
Simultaneously extend your right arm forward and left leg back against the band tension.
Squeeze your glute and core at full extension. Hold for 1 to 2 seconds.
Return to start under control.
Complete reps on this side, then switch band to left hand and right foot.
Use a light to moderate band. Aim for 10 to 12 reps per side.
Adds resistance to the bird dog
Builds anti-rotation core strength
Develops glute and shoulder stability
Excellent rehab and core exercise
Highly portable
Easy to scale by band thickness

description.en: The reverse hyperextension on a flat bench is a posterior chain exercise where you lie face down on a bench with your hips at the edge and legs hanging off, then lift your legs up to horizontal by squeezing your glutes and hamstrings. It targets the glutes and lower back without the spinal compression of squats or deadlifts.

en: Lie face down on a flat bench with your hips at the edge so your legs can hang off freely.
Grip the sides of the bench firmly for stability.
Let your legs hang straight down toward the floor. Brace your core.
Lift your legs up by squeezing your glutes and hamstrings. Keep legs relatively straight.
Continue lifting until your legs are parallel to the floor (or slightly higher). Squeeze hard.
Lower your legs back down under control.
Stop just before they touch the floor or hang fully.
Repeat for 12 to 20 reps. Add ankle weights for progression.
Targets the glutes and hamstrings without spinal compression
Excellent posterior chain finisher
Useful when no reverse hyper machine is available
Decompresses the lumbar spine
Easy to set up with just a bench
Useful rehab exercise after lower-back issues

description.en: The roll chest lying on floor is a self myofascial release drill for the chest. Lying face down with a foam roller under the pec and rolling slowly releases tightness that contributes to forward shoulder posture.

en: Lie face down on the floor.
Place a foam roller under one side of the chest near the shoulder.
Extend the working arm out to the side.
Brace the body on the other forearm.
Keep the working chest relaxed over the roller.
Roll the chest slowly over the roller.
Pause on tender spots for several breaths.
Cover the upper inner and outer chest then switch sides.
Releases the chest.
Improves shoulder posture.
Reduces front body tightness.
Useful after pressing work.
Joint friendly release.

description.en: The side lunge adductor stretch is a standing stretch where you take a wide stance and shift your weight to one bent leg, keeping the other leg straight. The straight leg gets a deep adductor stretch while the bent leg also stretches in a lateral squat position. It is functional and dynamic, useful as both warm-up and cooldown.

en: Stand with feet much wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward.
Place your hands at your chest or on the floor in front for support.
Shift your weight to your right leg by bending your right knee and sitting back on that side.
Keep your left leg straight with the foot flat on the floor.
Lower your hips as low as comfortable. Feel the deep stretch through your left inner thigh.
Keep your chest up and back flat.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. Breathe deeply.
Shift to the opposite side and repeat.
Deeply stretches one adductor at a time
Combines hip stretch with leg flexibility
Functional dynamic stretch
Excellent warm-up or cool-down
No equipment needed
Builds hip mobility for squats

description.en: The sitting sumo right twist stretch combines a deep sumo squat with a right torso rotation. The position opens the hips, obliques, and chest in one stretch.

en: Stand with the feet wide and toes turned out.
Lower into a deep sumo squat keeping the chest tall.
Rest the elbows on the inside of the knees.
Brace the core and place the left hand on the floor in front.
Reach the right hand up toward the ceiling.
Rotate the torso to the right following the hand.
Open the chest and feel the stretch through the obliques.
Hold the stretch for the desired duration.
Opens the hips and adductors.
Stretches the obliques through rotation.
No equipment needed.
Improves squat depth.
Excellent warm up before lower body work.
Carryover to thoracic mobility.

description.en: The sitting wide leg adductor stretch (also called the seated straddle stretch) is performed sitting on the floor with both legs extended wide apart. Folding forward over the legs deeply stretches the adductors, hamstrings, and lower back. It is a classic flexibility-building stretch used in dance, gymnastics, and martial arts.

en: Sit on the floor with both legs extended straight in front. Sit up tall.
Open both legs out to the sides as wide as comfortable. Toes point up.
Sit up tall with chest lifted. Place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Slowly walk your hands forward, hinging at the hips with a flat back.
Lower your torso forward as far as your flexibility allows.
Feel the deep stretch through your inner thighs, hamstrings, and lower back.
Hold for 30 to 60 seconds. Breathe deeply.
Avoid bouncing — let gravity deepen the stretch over time.
Deeply stretches the adductors and groin
Stretches the hamstrings and lower back
Builds long-term flexibility for splits
Calming and restorative
No equipment needed
Used in dance, gymnastics, and martial arts

description.en: The spine backbend stretch is a standing spinal extension where you place your hands on your lower back and gently arch backward, extending through the entire spine. It opens the front of the body, counteracts the rounded posture caused by sitting, and improves spinal extension mobility.

en: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Place both hands on your lower back with fingers pointing down for support.
Brace your core gently. Squeeze your glutes.
Lift your chest and slowly arch backward, extending through your entire spine.
Use your hands to support your lower back as you bend.
Look up if comfortable, but keep your neck long.
Hold for 5 to 15 seconds. Breathe deeply.
Slowly return to upright. Repeat 2 to 5 times.
Improves spinal extension mobility
Opens the entire front body
Counteracts sitting posture
Decompresses the spine
Quick and accessible
No equipment needed

description.en: The squat hold calf raise combines a bodyweight isometric squat with calf raises. Holding a parallel squat position throughout, you raise and lower onto your toes. The squat hold loads the quads while the calf raises build the lower legs in one efficient combo with no equipment required.

en: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold your arms out for balance or place hands on hips.
Squat down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Hold the parallel squat position throughout the set.
Raise both heels off the floor, lifting onto the balls of your feet.
Squeeze your calves hard at the top of the raise.
Lower your heels back down with control.
Continue raising and lowering your heels while holding the squat.
Trains calves and quads simultaneously
Builds isometric quad endurance
Forces calves to work under squat fatigue
No equipment required
Develops balance and proprioception
Useful as a warm-up or finisher

description.en: Standing leg circles draw circles with one leg while standing on the other. They mobilize the hip joint through its full range of motion — flexion, abduction, extension, and adduction in one circular path. Also known as hip CARs (controlled articular rotations).

en: Stand on your left leg. Hold a wall for balance.
Lift your right knee forward and up.
Circle your right leg out to the side, back, and around in a smooth circle.
Make the circles as large as your range allows.
Continue for 5 to 8 circles forward.
Reverse direction for 5 to 8 circles backward.
Switch legs and repeat.
Move with control — not momentum.
Full hip joint range of motion mobilization
Builds hip mobility in all directions
No equipment needed
Develops balance
Excellent warm-up before leg training
Promotes hip joint health

description.en: The suspender upper back stretch is a passive lat and upper back stretch using TRX. The lifter grips the handles, leans back with arms extended overhead, and lets the body hang. The TRX support allows a deep stretch through the lats and upper back without bar grip strength.

en: Set the suspension trainer at chest height.
Grip the handles with both hands.
Step the feet forward and lean back with arms extended.
Brace your core lightly and keep the body in a straight line.
Walk the feet forward more so the arms extend overhead.
Let the chest sink down between the arms.
Drop the head between the arms to deepen the stretch.
Hold with steady breath. Walk back to standing.
Strong lat stretch
Decompresses the spine
No bar needed
Useful cool down move
Builds shoulder mobility
Easy to scale by foot position

description.en: The suspension chin up is performed gripping suspension straps with an underhand (supinated) grip, then pulling your body up toward the handles. The supinated grip increases bicep involvement compared to a pull up, while the strap setup allows easy scaling by adjusting the body angle and foot position.

en: Anchor suspension straps overhead at a sturdy point.
Stand facing the anchor and grip the handles with palms facing you (underhand grip).
Walk your feet forward so your body angles back with arms extended.
Set your feet shoulder-width apart on the floor.
Brace your core and pull your shoulders back.
Pull your body up toward the handles by bending at the elbows.
Squeeze your biceps and lats at the top.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with control.
Underhand grip emphasizes biceps
Bodyweight back and bicep exercise
Easy to scale by changing foot position
Builds back and arm strength
Excellent for home or travel training
Strong functional pulling pattern

description.en: The toe walk is a simple endurance drill where you walk on the balls of your feet — heels never touching the ground. It builds calf endurance, ankle stability, and balance. It is used in physical therapy, athletic warm-ups, and combat sports footwork training.

en: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Rise up onto the balls of both feet (toes). Heels off the ground.
Begin walking forward in small steps while staying on your toes the entire time.
Keep your torso upright and core braced.
Walk for the desired distance (10 to 30 feet) or time (20 to 60 seconds).
Maintain a steady, controlled pace.
Turn around and walk back without lowering your heels.
Lower your heels only when finished.
Builds calf endurance
Develops ankle stability and proprioception
Used in physical therapy and rehabilitation
Useful for combat sports footwork
No equipment needed
Easy to scale by adjusting distance or duration

description.en: Tricep dips on the floor perform bench dip mechanics with hands placed on the floor behind you instead of on a bench. The floor limits the range of motion, making it a beginner regression for standard bench dips.

en: Sit on the floor with knees bent, feet flat. Place hands behind you with fingers pointing forward.
Lift your hips slightly off the floor.
Bend your elbows to lower your body toward the floor.
Lower until your glutes nearly touch the floor.
Press back up by extending your elbows.
Keep your back close to your hands throughout.
The floor limits range — this is easier than bench dips.
Aim for 12 to 20 reps.
Beginner regression for bench dips
No bench needed
Builds basic tricep pressing strength
Floor limits range for safety
Accessible anywhere
Progresses to bench dips

description.en: The weighted push up with vest is a standard push up performed with a weighted vest worn for added load. The vest distributes the weight evenly across the torso and lets the lifter add resistance without changing the push up form. It is a strong chest progression.

en: Put on a weighted vest with the desired load.
Begin in a high plank position with hands under the shoulders.
Set the body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and keep the back flat.
Lower the chest toward the floor by bending the elbows.
Stop just before the chest touches the floor.
Press back up to lockout.
Squeeze the chest hard at the top.
Strong chest builder
Adds load to push ups
Builds chest size
Useful push up progression
Strong vest move
Builds the triceps
